dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Then I'd better start walking.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: Be careful, child. I have outlived too many brave people.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: {player}'ll be fine, Hermit. Probably. Mostly.

dialogue.speaker: alchemist_qu
dialogue.text: If anything smells sweet in there, hold your breath. Sweet is how poison says hello.

objectives.text: Speak with the hermit

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: Good timing. Another minute and I'd have gone looking for you.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Is something wrong?

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: What the hermit said. Also, eat first. Nobody wins on an empty stomach.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: Just so.

objectives.text: Hear what Han Xue has to say

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: You look like someone with questions. I may even have answers.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Tell me.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: Tea is steeping. It will be ready when you are. Possibly sooner. Possibly next spring.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Please stop talking, Hermit.

objectives.choice_prompt: Han Xue asks you to vouch for a friend's examination, though you've never seen their work.

choices.text: Vouch anyway

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Breathe first, break rules second. You skipped a step.

reply.speaker: hermit_lan
reply.text: The bamboo bends. So did you. It is not always wrong.

choices.text: Refuse. Vouching must be honest.

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: By the book. The Law Hall would weep with joy.

choices.text: Vouch, for a favour later

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: I'll pretend I didn't see that.

quests.title: Salt for the Poultices
quests.summary: Elder Hua's poultices need salt from the old bandit road, of all places, gathered before the crates rot.

objectives.text: Hear Han Xue out

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: (guarded) {player}. People are saying things. I'm not asking. Yet.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: {player}! The juniors want to know if you're real. I told them barely.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Listen carefully, because I'll only say it twice. Bring me spirit herbs from the hidden valley.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: Senior Sister, did you eat? You never eat. Here, half a bun. The bigger half.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: ...Thank you. Don't tell anyone.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: I don't do speeches. Walk faster.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Leave the worrying to me for once.

objectives.text: Pick up spirit herbs near the hidden valley
See Han Xue again

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Every day you surprise me a little less. That's a compliment.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Just doing my part.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: The forest noticed. So did I. We are both very old and very hard to impress.

dialogue.speaker: watcher_pei
dialogue.text: I'll log it. 'Disciple returned. Victorious. Somewhat muddy.'

objectives.choice_prompt: The spirit herbs came from a hermit's plot, and the hermit isn't home.

choices.text: Leave payment and a note

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Sensible. Boring. Sensible.

choices.text: Take only what the task needs

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: You and the precepts. A love story.

reply.speaker: watcher_pei
reply.text: (to Han Xue) That's exactly what the precepts say! I memorised them!

choices.text: Take everything

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: (quietly) That was cold, {player}. Even for a war.

reply.speaker: watcher_pei
reply.text: (tugging Han Xue's sleeve) Is that allowed?

quests.title: The Shrine's Second Face
quests.summary: The ruined shrine in the clearing has more than one carving beneath its moss, if you look with a patient eye.

objectives.text: Search the alchemist's cottage

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Beneath the moss, a second face is carved into the old shrine stone, worn nearly smooth, wearing an expression like grief.

objectives.text: Stoke the pill furnace

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The pill furnace breathes out heat like a sleeping beast. Inside, a batch of pills turns slowly in the glow.

objectives.text: Compare notes with Wei Tong

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: You fight like the mountain taught you personally.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: That's twice this month you've made me proud. Stop it. It's unsettling.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Please stop. My ears are turning red.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: Ah. The kettle can stop worrying. It has been worrying since you left.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: Dumpling, my sword, is ready. I'm ready. My stomach is always ready.

objectives.choice_prompt: A dead courier's satchel holds silver for Blood Moon informers, and their names.

choices.text: Burn the names; they were desperate

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: Of course you did. You always do. It's infuriating.

choices.text: Give the names to the magistrate

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: Rules are like recipes. You followed it exactly.

choices.text: Keep the silver

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: Remind me never to owe you money.

quests.title: The Harvest Settles
quests.summary: With the moonbell dried and stored, your qi settles into something steadier, tempered by the forest's slow patience.

objectives.text: Speak with Elder Hua

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Fifth layer. The forest taught you that, as much as I did. Don't tell Elder Mo I said so.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: On my way.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: Be careful, all right? I don't want to eat your share of dinner. I'll do it, but I won't enjoy it.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Worry is a fine servant, Wei Tong. A poor master.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Breathe in for four before you go. Your qi runs hot when you hurry.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: People keep thanking me for things you did. It's getting embarrassing.

objectives.text: Consolidate your cultivation at the giant banyan

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You breathe in for four, hold for four. Qi gathers below your navel like water in a cupped hand.

objectives.text: Return to Elder Hua

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: That settles one worry. Only a hundred left.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Any time.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: And your heart, while you did it? Still? Or thrashing like a fish?

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: A fair question. I would like to hear the answer too.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: Look at {them}, all serious. Smile, {junior}! It confuses the enemy.

objectives.choice_prompt: A wandering cultivator offers you a pill that 'skips the hard parts'.

choices.text: Refuse. Your foundation must be honest.

reply.speaker: elder_hua
reply.text: Order is a kindness too, when it is fair.

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: Rules, rules. Fine. You're right. Again.

choices.text: Take it to the Medicine Hall to be tested

reply.speaker: elder_hua
reply.text: Sensible. Neither the soft road nor the hard one.

choices.text: Swallow it. Power is power.

reply.speaker: elder_hua
reply.text: A crooked road can still arrive. Mind that it does.

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: I didn't see anything. Nobody saw anything.

bonus.note: Grateful people press medicine into your hands.
Frightened people pay you to go away. You take it.
The Law Hall records your conduct with approval.
Rules bent, lessons learned the hard way.

quests.title: No Salt in Qingshi
quests.summary: Qingshi has had no salt for a month. Constable Du asks the sect for help, and Elder Mo sends you and Han Xue down the mountain.

objectives.text: Go and see Elder Mo

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Qingshi has had no salt in a month. Bandits on the road. The Sect Master is still sealed away, so I'm sending you.

dialogue.speaker: tang_ling
dialogue.text: Elder Mo is right. I checked the annals. Twice.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Right. Then I'll go.

dialogue.speaker: tang_ling
dialogue.text: The little ones tell stories about you, {senior}. Good ones!

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Han Xue goes too. Don't argue. She's a better cook and a worse liar than you.

objectives.text: Read the notice board at the town gate

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Qingshi's gate is open, but the market beyond it is half empty. A child is licking a salt-lick meant for oxen.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You read the notice board from corner to corner. Someone has crossed out a name and written a warning beside it.

objectives.text: Meet Constable Du at the town gate

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Cultivators. Good. Salt's gone, tempers are short, and last night someone boiled seawater they don't have.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I came as soon as I could.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: Constable, you owe me for three bowls of noodles.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Put it on the magistrate's account, Madam Fang.

dialogue.speaker: captain_lei
dialogue.text: Should my men go first? They're very brave. From a distance.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Caravans vanish on the forest road. Iron-Fang's leftovers, the carters say. Led by a man with a scar like a canal.

objectives.choice_prompt: Something valuable lies here, unclaimed: a purse of spirit stones.

choices.text: Report it to the sect

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: The magistrate would approve. So do I.

choices.text: Leave it for whoever lost it

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: The whole street will hear of this.

reply.speaker: captain_lei
reply.text: (to Constable Du) The whole street will hear of this kindness.

choices.text: Pocket it quietly

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: Bold. Very bold.

reply.speaker: innkeeper_fang
reply.text: Ha! Don't let the magistrate hear.

quests.title: Tallies at the Warehouse
quests.summary: Merchant Jin keeps the guild's salt tallies. He is nervous, overdressed, and suddenly very keen to be helpful.

objectives.text: Answer Merchant Jin's summons

dialogue.speaker: merchant_jin
dialogue.text: Salt, salt, everybody asks me about salt. The guild lost four caravans. Four! I'm practically a victim.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Then I'd better start walking.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Want company? No? Good. I have forms to practise. Call if you need me.

dialogue.speaker: merchant_jin
dialogue.text: Here, look at the tallies. Every wagon, every weight. I've nothing to hide. Please stop looking at my crates.

objectives.text: Head to the guild warehouse

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The warehouse yard is stacked with empty salt barrels. Somebody has scrubbed the stamps off half of them.

objectives.text: Search the guild's salt tallies

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The tallies are neat and honest, except for one column, marked with a crescent, where the numbers are far too round.

objectives.text: Show Han Xue what you found

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: A crescent. Same as Hong's ledger. Jin is still selling to somebody who signs with a moon.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: There you are. The noodles were getting cold, and so was my temper.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: You weren't worried, Madam Fang. You said so. Twice.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Not now. We can't prove anything and we need his wagons. But I'm writing it down. In ink.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Thank you for watching my back.

objectives.choice_prompt: A sealed jade slip lies here, stamped with another sect's seal.

choices.text: Return it to its sect unread

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Correct. Clean. Like a good stance.

choices.text: Read it first. Knowledge is knowledge.

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Reckless. It worked. Don't tell me how.

choices.text: Sell it to the highest bidder

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: (looks away) Right. Let's go.

reply.speaker: innkeeper_fang
reply.text: (to Han Xue, nervously) Should we... say something?

quests.title: Gossip Is Also Salt
quests.summary: Madam Fang's customers complain about the food, the bandits, and the magistrate, in that order.

objectives.text: Report to Madam Fang

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: My noodles taste of nothing and my customers taste of complaints. Bring back the salt, immortal, and eat free.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Easy enough. Famous last words, I know.

dialogue.speaker: captain_lei
dialogue.text: The militia will hold the street. The militia will mostly hold the street.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: You'll do no such thing, Captain Lei. Leave it to them.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: The carters drink here. They say the bandits don't take the salt. They take the salt and the carters. Then send the carters home.

objectives.text: Talk with Old Pan at the docks

dialogue.speaker: ferryman_pan
dialogue.text: Seen them. From the river. They camp in the old bandit camp in the bamboo, the one you burned last spring.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I have time. Go on.

dialogue.speaker: magistrate_zhou
dialogue.text: Do it lawfully, if you can. And if you can't, do it quietly.

dialogue.speaker: ferryman_pan
dialogue.text: That's sound, that is.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: Eat before you go. Nobody ever fought well on an empty stomach and a full head.

dialogue.speaker: ferryman_pan
dialogue.text: Came back like weeds. They're thinner now. Hungrier. Hungry men are dangerous and sad in equal parts.

objectives.text: Find Magistrate Zhou at the county granary

dialogue.speaker: magistrate_zhou
dialogue.text: The yamen has issued a strongly worded proclamation. It is nailed to the gate. It uses the word 'forthwith' twice.

dialogue.speaker: ferryman_pan
dialogue.text: River's high. Fares are higher. But for you, only very high.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I'm not laughing. I'm breathing strangely.

dialogue.speaker: merchant_jin
dialogue.text: If you need anything bought, sold or quietly moved, you know where the warehouse is.

dialogue.speaker: magistrate_zhou
dialogue.text: I, ah, have also put forty guards on the road. That was Constable Du's idea. The proclamation was mine.

objectives.choice_prompt: Magistrate Zhou admits the town's grain tally was fudged to feed the refugees.

choices.text: Keep it quiet. It fed people.

reply.speaker: magistrate_zhou
reply.text: The whole street will hear of this.

choices.text: Insist the books be put right

reply.speaker: magistrate_zhou
reply.text: The magistrate would approve. So do I.

choices.text: Take a cut for your silence

reply.speaker: magistrate_zhou
reply.text: (backing away) As you say, immortal.

quests.title: Guarding the Last Caravan
quests.summary: The last salt caravan of the season leaves the forest road at dusk. The bandits will not let it pass quietly.

objectives.text: Find Constable Du

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Last caravan of the season comes out of the bamboo at dusk. If it doesn't reach the gate, the town goes hungry.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I'll report back when it's done.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Your sleeve is torn. Either you fought a wolf or a thornbush. I'm betting thornbush.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Han Xue! Manners!

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: I've six men and a very old spear. You're the rest of the plan.

objectives.text: Ring the caravan bell at the gate

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The caravan bell clangs. Out on the road, wagons creak into a run, and shapes rise out of the ditches on either side.

objectives.text: Fight off the salt-road bandits

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They're on the fields! Get between them and the wagons!

objectives.text: Break the salt-road bandits at the night market

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A shout goes up. The salt-road bandits have found you first.

objectives.text: Go back to Constable Du

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Every barrel's in. Not one carter hurt. I'm going to write this down in the good ink.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: They weren't fighting to kill. They wanted the carters alive.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Tell me the truth. Did you hesitate at any point? Where?

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: (to Constable Du, low) Are we sure about this? You've heard what people are saying.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Then I'll ask the carters what they were for. Quietly, over a cup of Madam Fang's awful tea.

objectives.choice_prompt: Among the fallen bandits: a boy of fifteen, unhurt, too frightened to run.

choices.text: Send him home to his mother

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: (wiping away tears) Most of your kind wouldn't have bothered.

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: (to Constable Du) That's the {player} I know.

choices.text: Bring him to the sect to be judged

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: Proper. Very proper. Good.

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: (to Constable Du) Correct again. It's exhausting, isn't it?

choices.text: Make him carry your gear, unpaid

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: (says nothing, very carefully)

quests.title: The Carter Who Came Back
quests.summary: A carter taken last week walked home with a message pinned to his coat. It is addressed to the sect.

objectives.text: See what Widow Liu wants

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: Everyone knows your kindness. Here, have a peach.

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: (nervously) W-what can I do for you, immortal? Anything. Anything at all.

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: He came to the well at dawn, the carter. Walked like a man asleep. There was a letter pinned to him.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Do what Widow Liu says. It's a sound plan. I checked it for holes.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Then it's settled.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: Come back and tell me everything, or I'll have to make it up. My version is worse.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: If the Law Hall asks, I wasn't here and neither were you.

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: I read it. I shouldn't have. It isn't for me. It's for you.

objectives.text: Make your way to the town well

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The carter sits by the well, staring at nothing, a folded paper pinned to his coat with a bandit's knife.

objectives.text: Read the letter pinned to the carter

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Sect brats. Stay out of the bamboo, and the salt comes back. Come in, and my men stop being gentle. Gou.

objectives.text: Talk it over with Han Xue

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Gentle. They call that gentle. The man doesn't know his own name.

dialogue.speaker: captain_lei
dialogue.text: Good work, cultivator. I'll have the lads cheer. They're good at cheering.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Ha. Captain Lei's right. That was good.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: Gossip is free. Wine, noodles and advice are not. This is gossip.

dialogue.speaker: captain_lei
dialogue.text: (nervously, to Han Xue) Is it safe to talk in front of them?

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: He's afraid of something bigger than us. That's the only reason a bandit writes letters.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: My hands are still shaking. Give them a moment.

objectives.choice_prompt: A spirit crane is caught in a poacher's snare nearby.

choices.text: Free it and bind its wing

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: That's why people follow you, you know.

reply.speaker: captain_lei
reply.text: (to Han Xue) The whole street will hear of this kindness.

choices.text: Report the poachers to the sect

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Correct. Clean. Like a good stance.

reply.speaker: captain_lei
reply.text: (to Han Xue) Proper. Very proper. The magistrate will be pleased.

choices.text: Take it for its feathers

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: (looks away) Right. Let's go.

reply.speaker: innkeeper_fang
reply.text: (pales) Of course. Of course.

quests.title: Tracks Toward the Bamboo
quests.summary: The carters' tracks lead off the road and into the forest, toward the camp you burned in spring.

objectives.text: Check the fishing boat at the docks

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Wheel ruts leave the road at the river and turn toward the dark line of bamboo on the far bank.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The hull of the fishing boat has been patched in a hurry. Something scraped it, hard, from below.

objectives.text: Stop the salt-road bandits at the far forest gate

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Lookouts drop from the bamboo with sharpened poles. They are thin, and frightened, and very determined.

objectives.text: Scout the lookout rock

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: From the lookout rock you can see the old camp rebuilt: tents, fires, and a pen full of silent carters.

objectives.text: Share your findings with Han Xue

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They're holding the carters. Feeding them, even. Like livestock.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Or like hostages. Someone's holding their families. Now they're holding ours.

dialogue.speaker: headman_kuang
dialogue.text: The earth god will hear of this. Loudly. We'll light the big incense.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Don't encourage {them}, Headman Kuang. The head's big enough already.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Then we take them all home. Carters first. Answers second. The scarred man last.

objectives.choice_prompt: The bandits left a purse of spirit stones behind, and a wounded straggler.

choices.text: Return the stones to the people they robbed

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: You're too nice. It's annoying. I like it.

reply.speaker: headman_kuang
reply.text: (to Han Xue) The whole street will hear of this kindness.

choices.text: Turn stones and straggler over to the sect

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: You and the precepts. A love story.

choices.text: Pocket the stones and leave the straggler

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Remind me never to owe you money.

quests.title: The Pen of Carters
quests.summary: Before Gou can move his prisoners, you slip into the camp at night to open the pen.

objectives.text: Hurry to the old bandit camp

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The pen is a ring of stakes and rope. Inside, a dozen carters sit very still, listening to the fires.

objectives.text: Defeat the salt-road bandits at the old bandit camp

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Weapons up! This is going to get loud.

objectives.text: Cut open the carters' pen

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The ropes part. The carters don't run at first. They've forgotten how. Then one laughs, and they all run at once.

objectives.text: Tell Han Xue what you found

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They're out. Gou isn't in the camp. His tent is empty and warm.

dialogue.speaker: woodcutter_shu
dialogue.text: Bamboo grows faster than I cut. I've made my peace with it. The bamboo hasn't.

dialogue.speaker: woodcutter_shu
dialogue.text: My mother lights incense for you. She says it's the least she can do.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: He'll be back, and angry. Angry men are sloppy. Let's be the opposite.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: It's done. For now.

objectives.choice_prompt: One of the bandits is still alive, clutching a wound and begging for his life.

choices.text: Bind his wound and let him go

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Hm. Kind. Don't let it make you slow.

choices.text: Hand him over to face the law

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: By the book. The Law Hall would weep with joy.

choices.text: End it. He would have killed you.

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: That's not you. Or it didn't used to be.

choices.text: Make him swear to serve you, then let him run

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: I didn't see anything. Nobody saw anything.

reply.speaker: woodcutter_shu
reply.text: (to Han Xue) Bold. Don't tell the constable.

quests.title: A Scar Like a Canal
quests.summary: Gou's tent holds maps, a child's wooden toy and a list of names. The names are not his victims.

objectives.text: Go to the old bandit camp

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Gou's tent is neat as a soldier's. A map of the salt road, a carved wooden horse, and a long list of names.

objectives.text: Search Gou's tent

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Beside each name: a village, and the words 'held since'. Beside the last name: Gou's own mother. Held since spring.

objectives.text: Compare notes with Han Xue

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They're not stealing salt. They're paying a ransom with it. Salt, carters, whatever the moon asks for.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: The Blood Moon has their families. Just like the young one said.

dialogue.speaker: alchemist_qu
dialogue.text: I only explode things on purpose. Usually. Don't stand near the blue jar.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: That wasn't funny, Qu Wanqing. ...It was a little funny.

dialogue.speaker: huntress_meng
dialogue.text: Clean tracking. You'd make a decent hunter, if you ever stop being a hero.

dialogue.speaker: alchemist_qu
dialogue.text: You and your precepts. One day you'll bow to a door for being properly shut.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: This goes to Elder Mo. And the Sect Master, when she opens that door. I'm starting to hate that door.

objectives.choice_prompt: A dead courier's satchel holds silver for Blood Moon informers, and their names.

choices.text: Burn the names; they were desperate

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: That's why people follow you, you know.

choices.text: Give the names to the magistrate

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: By the book. The Law Hall would weep with joy.

reply.speaker: huntress_meng
reply.text: (to Han Xue) Proper. Very proper. The magistrate will be pleased.

choices.text: Keep the silver

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: (quietly) That was cold, {player}. Even for a war.

reply.speaker: alchemist_qu
reply.text: (to Han Xue, low) We should talk about that. Later.

quests.title: Gou the Scarred
quests.summary: Gou the Scarred returns to find his camp empty and his hostages gone. He has nothing left to bargain with, and nothing to lose.

objectives.text: Turn the drying racks at the hunter's lodge

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Torches below. Gou the Scarred is back, and he is not shouting. He is very quietly sharpening a blade on the empty pen.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Bundles of herbs hang from the drying racks, drying in neat rows. One bundle is the wrong herb entirely.

objectives.name: Gou the Scarred
objectives.text: Face Gou the Scarred at the old bandit camp

dialogue.speaker: bandit_gou
dialogue.text: You took my carters. Do you know what that costs me? Not silver. Not salt. My mother's dinner.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Then help us get her back instead. We're not the ones holding her.

dialogue.speaker: bandit_gou
dialogue.text: Nobody gets them back! Nobody! Pick up your sword, sect brat!

objectives.text: Join Gou the Scarred at the old battlefield

dialogue.speaker: bandit_gou
dialogue.text: Why... didn't you kill me?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Because you're not the one I'm angry at. Give Constable Du your men's names. All of them. And the villages.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Try not to trip over your own sword this time.

dialogue.speaker: bandit_gou
dialogue.text: Shut it, Han Xue.

dialogue.speaker: bandit_gou
dialogue.text: ...You're a fool. Iron-Fang would've gutted you. Fine. Fine. Names. For whatever good it does.

objectives.choice_prompt: Gou sits in the dirt, beaten, his men's names half-written. The carters he took want him punished.

choices.text: Spare him, and send him with the names to Du

reply.speaker: bandit_gou
reply.text: Kinder than the road ever was to me.

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: (to Gou the Scarred) That's the {player} I know.

choices.text: Hand him to Constable Du for judgement

reply.speaker: bandit_gou
reply.text: By the book. Fine.

choices.text: Break his sword hand so he never raids again

reply.speaker: bandit_gou
reply.text: That's the look I used to see in the water.

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: (muttering, to Gou the Scarred) That was cold.

quests.title: Salt on the Table
quests.summary: Qingshi has salt again. Madam Fang's noodles taste of something, and Gou sits in the yamen cell writing names.

objectives.text: Hear Madam Fang out

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: Salt! Noodles that taste like noodles! Free bowls for the heroes. Two each. I'm feeling reckless.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Then I'll go now, while the light holds.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Madam Fang, your gossip is faster than my runners.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: My gossip is paid in wine, Constable. Your runners aren't.

dialogue.speaker: apothecary_wang
dialogue.text: Half my shelves are empty since the trouble began. Medicine doesn't grow on shelves.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: (nervously, to Madam Fang) Is it safe to talk in front of them?

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: Constable Du has the scarred one writing in the yamen. Page after page. Villages I've never heard of.

objectives.text: Sit in the quiet of the town temple

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: In the clean temple, you breathe. A page of names drifts through your mind. Every name is somebody's mother.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Your qi steadies around the thought, and deepens. Not anger. Something slower, that will last longer.

objectives.text: Speak with Constable Du

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Forty-one names. Forty-one families held by the Blood Moon. The magistrate fainted. Then he got up and sent letters.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Tell me.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: Constable, you owe me for three bowls of noodles.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Put it on the magistrate's account, Madam Fang.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: My mother lights incense for you. She says it's the least she can do.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: I don't know where they're kept. But now I know they exist. That's how every case starts.

objectives.choice_prompt: Nearby, a junior's qi is running wild. Helping will cost you your meditation.

choices.text: Stop and steady their qi

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: (wiping away tears) Most of your kind wouldn't have bothered.

choices.text: Send for the elders; it's their duty
